speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the consultation. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia alongside a significant medical history. To begin our assessment, have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs in addition to the unsteadiness?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the sensation of looking "drunk" is very helpful. Given the clumsiness is worse on your right side, have you noticed any specific sensory changes like numbness or tingling in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The patient's history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, a known risk factor for PML, combined with new onset ataxia and clumsiness, is highly suspicious for this opportunistic infection. I recommend requesting MRI images of the brain immediately to confirm the diagnosis.
